## Purpose

Each `mustard` subcommand is exactly one module under `apps/cli/src/commands/`, named after the CLI verb in snake_case (`add.rs`, `config.rs`, `init.rs`, `install_grammars.rs`, `install_nerd_font.rs`). Every one of them exposes a single public flag struct declared `#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)] pub struct <Verb>Options` — a plain bag with one `pub` field per `#[arg]` in `cli.rs`, each field carrying a `///` line that echoes the flag's help text. The struct has no `impl` block, no builder and no constructor: `cli.rs` builds it inline in its dispatch arm and passes it by reference, which is why `Default` is derived (tests use `<Verb>Options::default()` or struct-update syntax such as `InitOptions { yes: true, ..InitOptions::default() }`). The entry function is the module's only other public item — `pub fn <verb>(path: &Path, options: &<Verb>Options) -> Result<()>` — and everything beneath it is a private free function; `config.rs` shows how thin that entry may legitimately be when the real rules live elsewhere (`git_flow::configure`). Progress is narrated with `println!` in short didactic lines; failures return `anyhow` errors with context rather than printing and continuing.

## Convention

- Folder: `apps/cli/src/commands/` — flat, no nested subdirectories.
- Extension: `.rs`, one snake_case module per CLI verb, registered in `commands/mod.rs`.
- File count: 6 — five subcommand modules plus `git_flow.rs`, which is the shared configuration routine `init` and `config` both call and therefore has no `Options` struct of its own.
- Naming: `<Verb>Options` is the rule; `InstallGrammarsArgs` is the single legacy `Args`-suffixed outlier — do not copy it for new modules.

## How to apply

Create `apps/cli/src/commands/<verb>.rs` opening with a `//!` block that names the invocation and states what the command does *and* deliberately does not do. Add `pub mod <verb>;` in alphabetical order to `apps/cli/src/commands/mod.rs` and a sentence describing it in that file's `//!` header. Declare the flag struct first, right after the imports, with `#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]` and one documented `pub` field per flag; add a field only when a matching `#[arg]` exists in the `cli.rs` variant — no speculative knobs. Then the entry function, whose signature is `(&Path, &<Verb>Options)` (a positional argument, when the verb takes one, sits between them as in `add(cwd, template_spec, options)`), returning `anyhow::Result<()>`; validate inputs early and `bail!` with an actionable message before touching disk. Keep helpers private and single-purpose: name validation (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, reject `..`) before any filesystem or network use, `mfs::create_dir_all` / `mfs::read_to_string` / `mfs::write_atomic` from `mustard_core::io::fs as mfs` for I/O, `fs_ops::read_json_object` plus `entry().or_insert_with(|| json!(…))` for settings merges, and a trailing newline on every serialized JSON write.

External tool probes are non-blocking by rule: `Command::new("x").arg("--version").output().is_ok_and(|o| o.status.success())`, degrading to printed install hints per platform — RTK's `probe_rtk` is the sole hard gate that exits `1`. Guard side effects under unit tests with `if cfg!(test) { return; }` so a clean CI runner never shells out to a package manager. No language or framework identifier may appear in these `.rs` files — language data belongs in `apps/cli/templates/grammars-suggestions.json`. Finish the module with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` using `use super::*;` and `tempfile::tempdir`, covering at least the refusal paths and the "user file survives" behaviour; `unwrap`/`expect` are allowed only inside that module.

## Examples

- Ref: `apps/cli/src/commands/init.rs` — `InitOptions { force, yes, dry_run }`, the `init` → `init_with_templates` split that keeps environment resolution out of install logic, and the fail-open tool probes.
- Ref: `apps/cli/src/commands/add.rs` — `AddOptions { force }`, early `bail!` guards, name validation, and `settings.json` merging via `read_json_object` + `mfs::write_atomic`.
- Ref: `apps/cli/src/commands/config.rs` — the minimal shape: `ConfigOptions { yes }` and a two-line entry function delegating to `git_flow::configure`.
